questions.question_text: Decide by substitution whether $(2,3)$ lies in the region defined by $y>2x-2$.

options.why: Reversed the comparison: $3$ is greater than $2$.
Swapped the coordinates, using $x=3$ and $y=2$ instead of $x=2$ and $y=3$.
Omitted the $-2$ in $2x-2$ when substituting $x=2$.

questions.solution_text:
Substitute $x=2$ and $y=3$: $2(2)-2=2$.
$3>2$ is true, so $(2,3)$ lies in the region.

questions.question_text: Decide by substitution whether $(1,0)$ lies in the region defined by $y\le -2x+2$.

options.why: Treated $\le$ as $<$; $\le$ includes points on the boundary.
Changed the constant $+2$ to $-2$, obtaining $-2(1)-2=-4$.
Used the point's $x$-coordinate $1$ as its $y$-coordinate instead of $0$.

questions.solution_text:
Substitute $x=1$ and $y=0$: $-2(1)+2=0$.
$0\le 0$ is true, so $(1,0)$ lies on the included boundary and is in the region.

questions.question_text: Decide by substitution whether $(2,-1)$ lies in the region defined by $5x+2y\ge 12$.

options.why: Reversed the comparison: $8$ is less than $12$.
Used $y=1$ instead of $y=-1$, obtaining $5(2)+2(1)=12$.
Used the $x$-coordinate $2$ as $y$ instead of $-1$, obtaining $5(2)+2(2)=14$.

questions.solution_text:
$5(2)+2(-1)=10-2=8$.
$8\ge 12$ is false, so $(2,-1)$ does not lie in the region.

questions.question_text: Decide by substitution whether $(-3,4)$ lies in the region defined by $x<-3$.

options.text: Yes, because the boundary is included.
options.why: Treated the strict sign $<$ as $\le$, incorrectly including $x=-3$.
Dropped the negative sign from the boundary value $-3$.
Used the $y$-coordinate $4$ instead of the $x$-coordinate $-3$ and reversed $<$ to $>$.

questions.solution_text:
The point has $x=-3$.
$-3<-3$ is false, so $(-3,4)$ lies on the excluded boundary and is not in the region.

questions.question_text: Decide by substitution whether the origin $(0,0)$ lies in the region defined by $y<x-2$.

options.why: Reversed the comparison: $0$ is greater than $-2$.
Changed the constant $-2$ to $+2$.
Replaced the given sign $<$ with $>$.

questions.solution_text:
Substitute $x=0$ and $y=0$: $0<0-2$, giving $0<-2$.
This is false, so the origin does not lie in the region.
